column1: # canopy's options table. Every tmux option canopy sets, with the value it
# ships, in one place, so that "what can I change, and what is it now?" has an
# answer that is not "read four layer files".
# `canopy config` reads this and prints each option's live value against the
# default below. docs/04-configuration.md cites it. A test asserts that every
# `set -g @...` in the shipped layers appears here with the same default and
# the same source, so a layer edited without this file is a failing test
#   default      the value canopy ships. `-` means the empty string
#   source       where that default comes from, which decides what an unset
#                  layer      a conf.d layer sets it, so unset means the
#                             layer did not load, and `canopy config` says so
#                  code       the default lives in a script, so unset is
#                  generated  computed at load from what is on the machine,
#                             so there is no fixed value to compare against
#   group        what it is about, and how `canopy config` groups its output.
#   description  one line, for somebody who does not already know
# Not here, because they are per-machine facts rather than settings: the
# `canopy caps` from what it finds on the machine. See the capability model in

column5: description
Draw the battery pill. Any value but `off` is on; a machine with no battery draws nothing either way
Draw the network pill. Any value but `off` is on
Left end-cap glyph for a status pill, U+E0B6. A machine without a nerd font sets this and @pill_r to empty in user.conf, and every segment renders as plain text with no caps
Right end-cap glyph for a status pill, U+E0B4
Background, used as the text colour inside a filled pill
Foreground, the status line's default text colour
The session pill
The current window's pill
The clock pill
Inactive windows and the date pill
Window names that are not current
Anything wrong: a low battery, a disconnected network
Restore the last save when a new server starts. Upstream continuum defaults this to off, which is why canopy sets it: without it every save is written and none is ever read
Minutes between automatic saves. 0 stops autosaving entirely
Where save files are written. Moving it to an empty directory is how a reboot silently comes back with nothing
Key that saves now. Moved off resurrect's own C-s, which would take canopy's prefix
Key that restores the last save over this server
Restore a Neovim pane from its Session.vim rather than as a bare editor
canopy's save strategy, as a path relative to resurrect's own strategies directory. This is what rewrites an agent pane's saved command into the one that resumes its conversation
Which saved commands resurrect is allowed to replay. Computed at load from the adapters on disk, because an adapter is a file a user adds rather than a name canopy knows in advance

Upper bound in milliseconds on the wait put in front of each restored agent command, so ten panes do not launch ten agents at once. 0 turns it off. The default is in lib/resume.sh rather than a layer, because a save has nobody to report a bad value to
Carries no behaviour. It is the probe that proves the core layer loaded and that user.conf overrides it
Set once the core layer has appended its terminal settings, so re-sourcing the config does not append them a second time
